title: Historical Metric Rectifier: Idempotent Stitcher for Console Analytics Backfills
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: We have multiple historical windows where console usage metrics (route-level latency, token counts, model selection breakdown) are incomplete or inconsistent due to past schema drift, partial ingest failures, and deduplication gaps. Ad-hoc backfills have caused duplicated events in the warehouse and skewed cost/latency dashboards. Goal: Build an idempotent, checkpointed 'Stitcher' service that can: (1) reconstruct canonical metric aggregates from archival event segments and compacted summaries; (2) safely re-run partial windows without producing duplicate rows; (3) produce audit logs and a dry-run diff; (4) integrate with rollout gating to slowly apply corrections to production dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Stitcher can process a 30-day historical window (1B events) in under 12 hours using our standard fleet size
All outputs are idempotent: re-running the same input + checkpoint does not change final aggregates
Backfill runs produce a signed dry-run diff report that matches ground-truth sampling (95%+ match on sampled buckets)
Dashboards accept a switch to 'apply-corrections' toggle; toggle flips from preview to live within 1 hour and is reversible
End-to-end QA: no visible double-counting on production cost breakdowns after staged rollout
design_notes: Core idea: treat backfills as deterministic transforms over ordered event segments. Produce a stable, canonical event key (customer_id + route + monotonic-event-hash) and apply idempotent write semantics into the metrics store
Input sources: archival S3 event segments (time-partitioned) + compacted CSV summaries exported by the streaming tier. Avoid reading raw Kafka offsets for historical windows to reduce coupling.

Execution model: orchestrator service launches parallel Stitcher workers that claim non-overlapping time shards. Shards tracked in a central checkpoint store (Postgres) with optimistic leasing and tombstones for completed shards

Dedup strategy: compute canonical event fingerprint and use upsert semantics into a write-optimized metrics table with 'source_run_id' and 'fingerprint' columns. Use composite primary key (metric_key, day, fingerprint) + last_write_run to make operations idempotent
Ordering: within a shard, workers preserve event-order only for causal operations (per-customer); aggregate math is associative so per-shard aggregation reduces cross-shard coordination
Failure recovery: workers checkpoint progress at sub-shard intervals (~5m). On restart, worker replays from last checkpoint. Checkpoints are immutable once marked completed
Dry-run: by default Stitcher writes only into a sandbox schema and produces a signed diff (row-level and aggregate-level) stored in archival S3 for auditing
Performance knobs: vectorized parsing in Rust, SIMD-enabled aggregation, and optional partitioned MapReduce step when memory pressure high
Expose a 'reconciliation mode' which can re-hydrate KV caches used by the runtime so downstream runtime caches reflect corrected aggregates when applied
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Week 1): Unit tests + integration tests against small synthetic datasets. Add schema compatibility checks for archival segments
Phase 1 (Week 2): Run Stitcher in dry-run against a 7-day historical window. Validate diffs with sampling and manual QA. Share diff with Observability and Billing teams
Phase 2 (Week 3): Staged apply to internal dashboards (non-customer facing) behind 'apply-corrections' toggle. Monitor for anomalies for 48h
Phase 3 (Week 4): Apply to production dashboards for low-risk customers (10% sample). Validate rollback path
Phase 4 (Week 5): Global apply if no regressions. Publish run metadata and audit logs to the compliance bucket
tasks: T1: Implement canonical fingerprint generator (Rust lib) - ENG
T2: Build Stitcher worker that reads archival segments and emits aggregated rows into sandbox schema
T3: Checkpoint store schema + lease API in Postgres
T4: Dry-run diff reporter and S3 export
T5: Metrics and tracing for per-shard throughput, latency, error rates
T6: QA harness + sampled ground-truth comparer
T7: Console toggle and rollout gating UI (coord with console-ux PM)
T8: Runbook and rollback docs for SRE/Observability
